title: Eagles - Hotel California (full song) - VALIDATED, and the case that calibrated the seventh gate
source: Ultimate Guitar official chord chart + real bs_roformer_sw stems of the full song (6.45 min, 16kHz mono: guitar, bass, drums, other)
notes: THIS IS THE STUDIO VERSION, in Bm, and it MATCHES the chart. (The separately-supplied 62s solo excerpt is a different arrangement in Dm - see eagles-hotel-california-solo.json. Do not confuse them.)
RESULT: all 8 chart chords found, ZERO spurious roots, ZERO missed roots. 13 distinct names against the chart's 8; the extras (A5, B, B5, E5, G5) are quality errors on correct roots. 102 chips.

THE SEVENTH GATE IS CALIBRATED BY THIS SONG, and CHORD_SEVENTH_ABSENCE_RATIO=0.2 PASSES. The chart uses plain F# (verse line 1) and F#7 (verse line 4), once each per cycle, so a correct read shows both in rough balance. Measured: F# 115 beats / 15 chips (57%), F#7 88 beats / 11 chips (43%). Both present, neither swallowing the other. From 1:21 the ribbon reads B5 F# A E G D Em F#7 - the chart's verse exactly, bar for bar.
That closes the question left open by CD-9, which deliberately did not tune this constant because the only charts available then contained no sevenths at all and could push it in one direction only.

KNOWN DEFECT this song exposes, NOT fixed: the BPM readout is DOUBLE. analyze_track's start_bpm=140 prior (BT-01) drives this 75bpm song to 144.2. Priors of 90 or 100 read it correctly, and also keep Airbourne (115) and Empty Rooms (99) correct - but they re-break the songs the prior exists for: Phantom of the Opera reads 86.1 at priors 75/90/100 and only 172.3 at 140. A single global prior cannot serve a 75bpm ballad and a 172bpm metal song; this is the classic tempo-octave ambiguity and needs a real disambiguator, not a different constant. Users can correct it with the app's own half/double tempo control.
Note the chord lane survives the double grid reasonably: a bar is simply 8 grid-beats instead of 4, and 81% of chips land within one beat of a bar boundary (85% with the correct grid).

UNEVEN CHIP SPACING IN THE FIRST ~80 SECONDS (user report: 'from 1:21 on looks spot on but the first part is screwy'). The boundary is real and reproduces exactly: chip lengths before 1:21 are 2,7,9,8,3,5,3,13,3,5,7 beats; after, 9,7,9,8,8,8,7,9,8,8,8,8 - i.e. one bar each. Ruled out by measurement: beat-grid instability (CV ~0.035 everywhere, no early/late difference); the drums-free intro (drums do start at 0:50, and silencing drums produces MISSING chords, not uneven ones); the tempo error (the correct 75bpm grid leaves the early section just as ragged: 9,4,2,10,2,2,3,5); and harmonic texture density (chroma bins-per-frame is flat at 2.0-2.5 across the whole song). What DOES track the boundary is LEVEL: the intro builds from rms 0.010 to 0.030 right at 1:20, so early chroma has far worse signal-to-noise against separation bleed. Quiet passages give noisier chord evidence.
